conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-22_round4/round4.blend (saved from reactions5.blend), scene RD, one station per look (x from 120000, 40 m apart, order in tools/rd_order.json). Built by script (tools/b1.py to b4.py on tools/rdcommon.py) from the reactions-4 and reactions-5 specs where a look keeps what the owner liked, the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits, combo kits v3, r4 and r5, and the new kit vfx_round4_kit.fbx.
conventions.made: 2026-11-22 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the main body's ground point (y = 0): the body point 3 m out from the player along the line player to body. Pieces with on_player (and ribbons whose centre is player) are relative to the player's ground point. Offsets are world-aligned to the camera (it looks along Unity +z from -z, 55 degrees down).
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body (or in the bowl), p = on the player.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.blade_frame: The charged-blade looks swing a stand-in katana (vfxe3_katana) about the player: it and its sheaths (vfxe3_flameflag_a/b, iceteeth, watersheath, thornvine, stonespine, edgelight, venomcoat) share one frame with the pivot at the hilt end: the blade along local +x (Blender; Unity -x after the axis bake), grip 0 to 0.27 m, guard 0.27 to 0.30 m, blade 0.30 to 1.25 m, the edge facing local +y (Blender), the flat facing up. Their motion.orbit (centre_is player) is the swing: three cuts 0.45 s apart. In Unity, parent the sheath to the real weapon's blade bone with the same frame scaled to the blade length; the orbit keys are the mock-up of the weapon animation, not data to play.
conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (the toon stone and stand-in bodies excepted); no stop reaches pure white. The strip maker counts pure-white pixels per frame (white_check.json): every look is 0.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment, owner (the fourth-review comment, quoted, and the plan's direction), answer (how the look answers it), look (in words), revision_of where it replaces an earlier look, strip (the beats) and round.
conventions.timing_round4: Every round-4 look is 1.5 s (cause, impact, aftermath), on the 20 fps timeline with t 0 at frame 7; pieces with a visible end of 9 stay to the end of the effect.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies; 0 is the main body) the piece belongs to: it is placed about that body and shown on it. Restored from the pass's own specs (staging/blender/2026-11-22_round4/tools/specs_*.gltf) by AgentScripts/recipe_bodies.py, as the export wrote only follow_body and orbit.centre_is. Numbers in a piece's name are not bodies (spark15, heavechip4). Pieces on the player carry on_player instead.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Smoulder: "Its good, just the flames that spread to others should be the black and purple not the normal fire"
The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: real flickering FLAME shapes in black with violet edges, rising and licking like fire, not dark spikes or thorns.
looks.answer: Round 2. The black fire is drawn as real flame now. Its real flame burns, then the curse turns it: seven tongues of black flame stand round it, each a near-black flame in front of a slightly bigger violet one, so every tongue has a violet edge, flickering and swaying together like fire, with deep violet hearts at the foot; black licks with violet edges tear off the tops and rise every 0.11 s, and black flakes rise. The flare runs across the floor to the near enemy as nine tongues of black flame springing up one after another, flickering and sinking (no spikes lying on the floor); the near enemy flinches and catches the same black fire, with its own licks and a violet-black scorch.
looks.look: The cursed enemy's fire turns to black flame with violet edges, flickering and licking up it. It flares, black flame springs up across the floor to the near enemy, and that one catches the same black fire.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Thermal Shock: "Its pretty good but the ice explosion doesnt look great"
The plan (2026-11-22): a better ice explosion (the frozen flames shatter).
looks.answer: Option B (the flames freeze, then shatter) with a new explosion. Before the break, the fire trapped inside glows orange through cracks running up each frozen flame, and the frozen flames swell. Then they burst: 26 shards of flame-shaped ice of mixed sizes (a quarter of them big) are flung up and out unevenly, tumbling end over end; they land 0.9 to 2.6 m out, skid and lie scattered (never an even ring), with a spray of glittering chips. Steam bursts out and rises, the trapped fire flares free for a moment and sinks back to burning, embers escape upward, and the enemy judders with the shock.
looks.look: The burning enemy is caught by frost: each flame freezes mid-flicker into ice. Fire glows through cracks in the frozen flames, then they burst into big tumbling shards of ice that land and lie scattered; steam bursts, the trapped fire flares free, and it burns on.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Logan Stone: "the fall explosion doesnt really make sense and the enemy doesnt fall"
The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: a bigger stone that clearly falls ON the enemy, flattening it, with dust; not landing in front of it from the camera's view.
looks.answer: Round 2. The stone is bigger (2.5 m tall, 1.2 m across) and stands just BEHIND the enemy as the camera sees it, so when it topples it comes forward, toward the camera, down onto the enemy and over it. Two fat curls of wind rock it on the edge of its foot, harder the second time; the third tips it forward. It lands on the enemy at 1.12 s: the enemy is flattened under it (squashed to a fifth of its height), dust bursts out from under the stone all round, then the stone breaks into seven chunks that roll off it and sink back into the ground, and the enemy pops back up with a wobble by 1.5 s.
looks.look: A big balanced stone heaves up behind the unsteady enemy. Gusts of wind rock it on its foot, twice, and the third tips it forward down onto the enemy, flattening it in a burst of dust. The stone breaks and sinks away, and the enemy pops back up.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Chokedamp: "Its decent, might need some reworking though it kinda appears, and doesnt really make sense"
The plan (2026-11-22): the ground cracks, then a low, heavy dark-green damp seeps out and rolls around the legs; enemies cough and stagger as it rises to the waist, then it sinks.
The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: soft see-through fog that rolls and thins, with no bush or lump shapes; Unity should draw it as real soft fog.
looks.answer: Round 2. The damp is soft fog now, with no lumps: every piece of it is a soft-edged see-through fog card (rd_fogcard: dark green, densest in the middle and fading to nothing at its edge). The ground splits and cracks run to the two near enemies; the damp seeps up out of the cracks as flat cards creeping along them, lies low round each enemy's legs as a bank of overlapping cards that drift round (rolling) and breathe, rises to the waist as upright cards facing the camera that roll round and thin while they cough little soft puffs and stagger, then sinks back and thins away as the cracks close. Unity: draw it as real soft fog (soft particles or a fog-card shader with a radial fade and depth fade), not meshes.
looks.look: The ground cracks under the shaken, poisoned enemy and the cracks run to the near ones. A soft, see-through dark-green damp seeps out of them and rolls round their legs, rising to the waist as they cough and stagger, then thins and sinks back into the cracks.
looks.unity_note: Draw the damp as real soft fog: soft particles or a fog-card shader (camera-facing or flat cards, radial alpha fade to 0 at the edge, depth fade where they meet bodies and floor), dark green, about 40 to 60% opaque at the centre. The Blender cards (e3k_disc with rd_fogcard) only mock the placement and timing.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Breath Taken: "This still is random black explosions and not really reading like black wind"
The plan (2026-11-22): near-black wind curls with violet edges sweep round the enemy, pull a pale wisp of breath from its mouth and swallow it.
looks.answer: No bursts at all now: it is all wind. Six near-black curls of wind with thin violet edges sweep in round the enemy as open spirals, tightening and turning about it. A pale blue-grey wisp of breath is pulled out of its mouth along the wind, spiralling up and out with puffs of breath that shrink as they go; then four tight black curls close on the end of it and swallow it, the wisp is erased from the mouth outward, and the black wind whips away in curls. The enemy doubles over as its breath is taken and straightens, breathless.
looks.look: Near-black curls of wind with violet edges sweep in round the enemy and tighten. A pale wisp of breath is pulled out of its mouth along the wind; the black curls close on it and swallow it, then whip away.

owner: 2026-11-21 (fourth review), Glint: "The concept is good, but the beam on the wizard enemy sucks"
The plan (2026-11-22): sharp gold-steel glints flash across the armour one at a time, then a reflected flash blinds; no standing beam.
The owner on the round-4 strip (2026-11-22), through the coordinator: bigger warm gold-steel glints and a stronger gold flash; never white.
looks.answer: Round 2. No beam or ray anywhere. On the Sundered, Marked enemy (dagger and star kept) six big, sharp four-point glints in a warmer gold-steel (rd_goldsteel: 0.98, 0.7, 0.28) flash across its armour one at a time, 0.11 s apart, half again as big as before, each with a sheen sliding across the plate. Then the light catches the dagger's point full on: a strong warm-gold flash (rd_flashgold: 1.0, 0.6, 0.12), half again as big, with twelve short sharp gold rays for 0.22 s, and the two near enemies are blinded: a gold flash in the eyes, they recoil and turn away, gold motes drifting off them. Nothing is white.
looks.look: Big gold-steel glints flash across the marked, Sundered enemy's armour one at a time; then the light catches its dagger's point in a strong gold flash that blinds the enemies near, who recoil.
